brief:
The documentary Naza has drawn international media and political attention following its Special Jury Prize win at the Venice Film Festival, Palestine News Network reported, even as the film remains unavailable to broader audiences. The award has intensified scrutiny of the film's historical claims and methodology.

Dr Sania El-Husseini's analysis connects Naza to broader questions about documentary practice and historical representation, examining how the film treats testimony and evidence in relation to events like those at Tantura. The film has become a focal point for debate over how Israeli documentaries address contested historical narratives.
dek: The Israeli documentary Naza attracted considerable international media and political attention after winning the Venice Film Festival’s Special Jury Prize, despite not yet having reached the wider public.
title: Israeli film Naza wins Venice prize amid historical debate
